findings.gate: Craft core: causal legibility; charter 4.1 (positions must hold and the sequence must be drawable from the text alone)

draft_evidence.quote: Karis coiled the cord. Seln came back up the slope from the stakes with nothing in his hands.

comparison_evidence.quote: The five of them stood on the crest above a cordon of iron round a circle eight hundred meters across

findings.consequence: The post-council gesture ledger at line 131 is the only span in the chapter that still runs on the pre-repair staging, and it now contradicts the council twice over. Seln is on the crest for the council — line 105 says everyone on the crest knew whose the silence was, line 107 counts five of them there, and line 115 gives Seln a speech in it — and then, after the decision is taken and 'Nobody crossed the line' has landed, he 'came back up the slope from the stakes', arriving at a place he has already spoken from. In the same sentence run Karis coils a cord she coiled at line 85. This was byte-identical in r2 and the r2 report did not raise it, so it is not introduced by this repair; but r2's line 87 sent the pacing party up the slope and left Seln alone below, which gave the beat somewhere to stand, and r3's line 87 now sends the four along the line to Seln instead, so the last staging that supported line 131 is gone. A reader following the chapter's own geography — which this chapter asks them to do more than any other in the book — hits it at the point the chapter is asking them to feel the stop.
findings.repair_target: At line 131, retire the two stale gestures and keep the paragraph's real work, which is the honest count ('three floors entered, one paced from outside') and the four small closing postures. Either drop 'Karis coiled the cord. Seln came back up the slope from the stakes with nothing in his hands.' and let the paragraph run from the count into Lira shifting the crossbow, or replace them with crest-side beats — Karis putting the coiled cord away, Seln standing at the crest's edge looking down the stake-line into the dark with nothing in his hands. Do not move the council: lines 105, 107, 115 and 119 place it on the crest and are load-bearing for the silence. The ascent itself does not need staging; the section break at line 103 carries it, and lines 131 and 133 confirm the crest on the far side.

findings.gate: Charter 3.1 (the cataloguing narrator's counts must hold); craft core: causal legibility

draft_evidence.quote: she stopped, and looked back up at the five of them on the crest, and said nothing, and went on.

comparison_evidence.quote: "Line," Karis said, and it was not a question, and she was already off the ridge's crest with the cord.

findings.consequence: The party is five. At this moment two of them are on the slope — Karis, who is off the crest with the cord at line 77, and Lira, who is doing the looking — so three are on the crest: Cael, Brom and Seln. 'The five of them on the crest' is short by the two people the sentence is about. The chapter uses 'the five of them' elsewhere as a floating name for the crew (lines 7, 107, 119) and it works in those places because the whole crew is where the sentence puts it; here the group label is doing double duty as a position, and the position is wrong. In a chapter whose subject is a count taken carefully in bad light, a miscount two lines before the pacing costs more than its size. Pre-existing in r2 and outside the repair's scope; raised now because the recheck's positional pass reached it.
findings.repair_target: At line 79, name the three who are actually up there or drop the number: 'looked back up at the three of them on the crest' is exact, and 'looked back up the slope at the others' costs nothing and cannot drift. Leave 'the five of them' at lines 107 and 119, where the whole crew is on the crest and the label is correct.

findings.gate: Charter 3.1 (the cataloguing narrator's counts must hold); craft core: causal legibility

draft_evidence.quote: the shape at the middle of four hundred meters of quiet that none of them had a word for

comparison_evidence.quote: a cordon of iron round a circle eight hundred meters across with a shape at its middle that the dark had

findings.consequence: Finding 010's repair fixed the one sentence it named and left the chapter carrying both idioms. Line 119's 'across four hundred meters of dark' is correct — that is the traverse from the line to the middle, and it is the distance Cael would walk. Line 133's 'at the middle of four hundred meters of quiet' is the other construction: 'at the middle of X' names the whole extent, and the whole extent is now eight hundred, said in those words eleven lines earlier. The two sentences are close enough together, and the chapter's arithmetic is load-bearing enough, that a reader who took line 107's number will stop at line 133. This is the same defect class 010 named, in the sentence 010 did not reach.
findings.repair_target: At line 133, restate as the traverse rather than the extent, in the idiom line 119 already uses: 'the shape four hundred meters in past the iron', or 'the shape at the middle of it', which inherits the circle from the cordon named in the same clause. Do not change line 119, which is correct as written, and do not reopen Karis's 'Four hundred. Near enough. Twice the radius.' at line 85.

concerns: The pronoun at line 83 is resolvable but not free. 'Karis a stride outside her ... and Cael at her shoulder writing it' puts two women in the clause run, and the second 'her' has to reach past Brom to find Karis. Context settles it — the count being written is the one Karis is saying aloud, and Ch10 puts Cael at Karis's shoulder for exactly that reason — but the sentence is read aloud in a scene where the difference between Karis's shoulder and Lira's is the difference between outside the line and on it, which is the thing finding 011 was protecting. 'Cael at Karis's shoulder writing it' costs one word and removes the reach. Recorded rather than raised because the repair target's own wording named Karis and the surrounding clause supplies her.

The 009 repair has one cost it does not spend a beat on. Once the iron is registered from the first cord, Lira is walking a boundary that somebody has already drawn on the ground a pace at a time, and the chapter has her keep calling it with her Arbiter for twenty cords without anyone remarking the redundancy. The prose supplies a reason for the silence — 'which nobody spoke of until the count was done, because a count was a count and Karis was saying it' — and it is the right reason for these people, and Karis measuring the line herself rather than trusting another surveyor's markers is her method as the book has established it. But the finding that lands at line 95, that the iron sits exactly where the Arbiter-line is, is now a confirmation the reader has been holding for two paragraphs rather than a discovery. That is a fair trade for the defect it removed; it is noted so a later pass knows the beat's weight moved.

Carried forward from r2 and still open at the planning layer: Karis's 'Three days, or near it' at line 15 is right against the chapter's own datelines — the finding on the morning of the 121st, the ridge at dusk on the 123rd — and still differs from the packet's must_include parenthetical, the POV knowledge boundary, and the provisional Ch23 state block, all of which say two days. Reader consequence remains nil. The arc card and the state block should be brought to three, since the 123rd is load-bearing for Ch24's 'six days from the fourth site'.

Also carried forward from r2 and unrepaired, correctly: Karis's 'I don't know what it does to a Path at the line' at line 111 still sits slightly over its evidence, since Lira has spent twenty cords stepping half a stride in and out with her Arbiter going and coming. The next clause concedes it ('I know the line's where Lira said'), and the prescribed pacing method cannot be run without producing exactly that knowledge, so this is method residue rather than an author defect. If a later pass opens line 111 for any reason, 'past the line' closes it at no cost.

The chapter sits at 4,264 words against a 4,600 target — inside the band, and a thousand words under the 5,290 ceiling that Ch21 is pinned to. If the repairs above are taken, all three have headroom to be made by addition rather than substitution, which is the cheaper way to keep the fork and the council at their current weight.
strengths: The 009 repair took the third and cheapest of the three options and it was the right one. Option (a) would have restaged Seln's discovery ahead of Lira's line-call and cost the chapter its opening move; option (b) would have darkened half the cordon to hide it. Option (c) leaves every existing beat where it is and adds one clause, and the clause is in the chapter's own register: the iron arrives as a thing four people walk past twenty times and do not mention, 'because a count was a count and Karis was saying it'. That is a truer sentence about these characters than a discovery beat would have been, and it makes the cordon's scale land through the boots rather than through an announcement.

One word carries the whole restaging. 'Seln had found the stakes' becoming 'Seln had read the stakes' converts the section from a discovery nobody else could have missed into the professional supplying what the others could see but not price — the number, the stamp, the stroke-and-bar mark, the spacing, and the distinction between measuring a circle and marking one. Seln's fixed line lands harder for arriving as a reading, because 'That's not a survey' is now a correction of what everyone present already assumed they were looking at.

Line 87 quietly repairs a contradiction the r2 report did not flag. In r2, Karis 'came back up the slope' with Brom and Lira and the very next section had Seln 'on one knee in the frost when they came to him' — two directions in two lines. r3's 'They came back along the line in the dark, the four of them, with the stones marked behind them beside the iron' resolves the movement, gathers the four into one body, and puts the iron in the return sentence where it does a second turn of work. The repair was scoped to 009 and cleared a defect adjacent to it.

The 011 repair took the first option and left line 81 alone, which is the correct reading of the finding. Cael counts Lira's paces from the crest at line 81 because that count is visible and taken from above, and writes Karis's cords at her shoulder at line 83 because that count is audible and taken at her elbow — two different counts, two different instruments, two different positions, exactly as chapter-10.md:13 stages it. A less careful repair would have moved him once and broken the other.

The 010 repair is one word and stops there. 'four hundred meters across' becoming 'eight hundred meters across' fixes the arithmetic without touching Karis's radius idiom at line 85 or either 'twice the size' in the council, which is what the repair target asked for and what keeps the chapter's central number in the mouth of the person who measured it.

Diff containment is exact: five lines, 4,212 to 4,264 words, no drift into any unflagged span. Three repair cycles into this chapter, the fork, the council, the fixed lines and the closing log are still the sentences they were when they passed, which is the whole point of a targeted repair.
